PullRequest.Title: agent host: track the Git state of each folder of a session and find the repositories in it
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

**What:** The agent host keeps the Git state of every folder of a session of several folders, and finds the Git repositories inside them the way Source Control does. No visible change on its own: the agent host sessions provider maps this into the session model in a later PR.

**Changes:**
- `AgentHostGitStateService`: every folder but the first gets its own Git state, GitHub repository and branch pull request (folder scope). Folders that are not repositories are recorded in `vscode.nonRepositoryFolders`; a folder that leaves the session loses its state.
- Repository discovery, when a client sends a folder's `repositoryDetection` options (from its `git.*` detection settings): the folder's own repository, nested repositories and submodules, recorded in `vscode.sessionRepositories`, each with its own Git state.
- `IAgentHostGitService.findRepositories`: breadth-first like Source Control, no symbolic links, submodule paths kept inside their repository; every file system call is charged to a `RepositoryScanBudget`.
- Discovery runs outside the Git state refresh, once per session at a time: found again when folders or options change, when a repository is gone, every 60 s, and on a forced refresh after 30 s. Reads that finish for an outdated discovery record nothing.
- `getRepositoryRoot(…, { fresh: true })` reads the disk and corrects a stale cached root.
- Source Control parity: `git.ignoredRepositories` (absolute roots, or paths relative to each session folder), `git.scanRepositories` (relative paths, checked when subfolders are scanned), `git.detectSubmodulesLimit` (the first N submodules, default 10, no warning) and submodules of submodules. `.gitmodules` is read with a port of the Git extension's `parseGitmodules`, whose tests are ported too.

**Differences from Source Control (by design):**
- Safety caps (no file system call starts after 5 s, 10k file system calls, 64 repositories, 16 folders per discovery): the host scans without a user waiting on it and must stay bounded.
- No file watcher: repositories are found again every 60 s, when folders or options change, and on a forced refresh, as the host watches no workspace.
- No scan inside a found repository apart from its submodules: Source Control also opens other clones nested inside a found repository, but skipping them keeps the scan cheap, and at the default `git.repositoryScanMaxDepth` of 1 it rarely matters.
- `git.autoRepositoryDetection: openEditors` means no subfolder scan: the host has no editors.
- A folder's repository in a parent folder is always used (`git.openRepositoryInParentFolders` doesn't apply): the session folder is where the agent works.
- A session folder's own repository is always used, also when `git.ignoredRepositories` lists it: the host needs it for the folder's branch, worktree and changes.
- A checkout Git refuses as unsafe (`safe.directory`) is left out (and logged); Source Control lists it as unsafe and offers to open it.
- A negative `git.detectSubmodulesLimit` takes no submodules (Source Control's slice would take all but the last), and at most 64 are taken from one `.gitmodules` file; paths with a `.git` component, in any case, are never scanned.
- Out of scope: `git.detectWorktrees` (worktrees of other folders come with #350551).

**Notes for reviewers:**
- Bounds: at most 16 folders discovered (one `git rev-parse` each), one budget per discovery of 10k file system calls and Git checks of candidates, none started after 5 s (a deadline for starting calls, not a timeout on one already running), at most 64 repositories. A refresh starts at most 16 extra Git state reads, each starting three Git commands (so up to 48) before optional base and upstream probes.
- A folder with a `.git` entry is a repository only when Git opens a checkout rooted there. Pull requests found automatically for other folders and found repositories are recorded for that folder only, never as the session's latest outcome. A folder loses its recorded state once Git says it is not a repository, and its GitHub state once its remotes are read and none is on GitHub. A change of the detection options refreshes the session's Git state, and options changed while a scan runs are found once it settles. After a failed read of another folder, whether it is still a repository is read from disk, unless Git already said it is not one (an ordinary refresh runs no Git command for such a folder, a forced one runs one).
- Folder state saves are not awaited, so coalesced saves never hold a refresh, a discovery or a pull request lookup.
- `vscode.nonRepositoryFolders` is only written for sessions of several folders. A session without detection options that never recorded repositories skips the repository bookkeeping, an optimization.
- New changeset E2E tests discard a file in a session with a second, non-repository folder, with and without repository detection options.
- Per-repository changesets come in the next PR.
- The Discard refresh race fix this PR's E2E tests rely on landed separately in #350452.

## How to test

No visible change. Tests:
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/platform/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js"`: 18998 passing, 0 failing.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/conformance/agentHostConformance.integrationTest.ts`: 378 passing, 15 pending, 0 failing on ee63500ebc0.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/conformance/agentHostConformance.integrationTest.ts --grep "changeset|Changeset|discard|uncommitted|branch"` (changeset E2E): 50 passing, 7 pending, 0 failing on ee63500ebc0.

**Validation:** `pnpm run typecheck-client` and `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` pass.

Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @sandy081

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added await reaches _applyDiscoveredRepositories on every warm-cache refresh, which awaits all selected Git reads. The unchanged operation service explicitly awaits this refresh before publishing Idle and returning the operation result. The delay magnitude depends on checkout and disk size, not on an uncertain call path.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocesses, especially repository-wide git status and associated filesystem traversal
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each selected distinct checkout starts three initial Git commands plus optional base/upstream probes. Up to 16 discovered checkouts are awaited for a one-folder session; with gitCoalesceReads enabled commands share the global eight-read limiter, while the default false setting launches them without that limiter. Completion depends on the slowest read or on multiple limiter waves.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased changeset-operation response latency and prolonged Running status because unrelated large or slow checkouts block completion
Findings.PreviousBehavior: After a changesGitState operation, the refresh read the source checkout (and the session checkout when applicable); unrelated nested checkouts were not read before completing the operation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Once discovery is cached, completing the same operation also waits for passive state reads of up to min(unique discovered roots, max(0,16-(session folders-1))) unrelated checkouts. Unlike cold discovery, these warm reads are not background work.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added await at line 700 invokes _refreshSessionRepositories before the refresh event and refresh completion. Its new warm-cache branch at line 888 returns _applyDiscoveredRepositories, whose line 959 awaits Promise.all of discovered-root Git-state reads. No such discovered-repository work existed in the base refresh.
Findings.Title: Keep passive repository reads off changeset-operation completion
Findings.Impact: Discarding a file or another Git-changing operation in the primary checkout can remain Running until an unrelated discovered checkout finishes git status. Each Git command has a 30-second default timeout. This affects warm-cache sessions even though discovery itself is backgrounded.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostChangesetOperationService._executeChangesetOperation lines 489-506 awaits _refreshGitState before publishing Idle and returning. _refreshGitState lines 80-87 awaits the source/session refresh. AgentHostDiscardChangesOperationHandler line 109 sets changesGitState=true. The new _refreshSessionRepositories line 888 awaits _applyDiscoveredRepositories; lines 958-959 select and await discovered-root reads. AgentHostGitService._computeSessionGitState lines 1888-1906 resolves each root and runs status -b --porcelain=v2, remote -v, and symbolic-ref. _spawnGit uses the 30-second default timeout.
Findings.Recommendation: Publish and complete the authoritative source/session-checkout refresh without waiting for passive additional/discovered-checkout reads; run those reads in a coalesced background lane with the existing generation guards and announce their results separately.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The PR explicitly supports different folder paths within the same checkout, including a new test. _readGitState keys in-flight reads by the original folder URI, but _computeSessionGitState executes all probes at the resolved checkout root. The production schema defaults command coalescing to false, establishing duplicate processes rather than merely duplicate helper calls.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Duplicate git status traversals, Git subprocesses, filesystem reads, and status-output parsing
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For F additional eligible folder URIs under one checkout, F<=16, the default configuration starts F identical status commands plus F remote and F symbolic-ref commands before optional probes, even though the effective checkout/default-base group count is one. Command coalescing, when explicitly enabled, reduces overlapping identical probes but does not provide grouping in the default configuration.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Redundant CPU/filesystem work and subprocess contention on every refresh, increasing latency and reducing host throughput
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A session containing several subfolders of one monorepo read its primary checkout once during a session refresh; it did not automatically reread that checkout for each additional session folder.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The session now computes the same root-wide default-base Git state once per additional folder URI, although all those calls resolve to the same checkout and return equivalent data.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new folders.map loop at lines 752-759 calls _readGitState separately for every additional workingDirectory. Its unchanged in-flight key includes workingDirectory.toString(), so distinct subfolders of the same root are not grouped. The base session refresh did not enumerate and read these additional folders.
Findings.Title: Share additional-folder Git reads by checkout root
Findings.Impact: A multi-root workspace that opens several packages of the same large monorepo repeatedly runs repository-wide git status for each package after file changes or explicit refreshes. Sixteen additional folders can issue 48 initial commands for a single checkout, in addition to the primary refresh.
Findings.Evidence: The new test at agentHostGitStateService.test.ts around lines 3357-3385 uses file:///repo/sub and file:///repo/other and confirms both resolve to file:///repo. The added loop calls _readGitState at line 759 for each URI. _readGitState lines 1161 onward keys by original URI and baseBranchRef. AgentHostGitService.getSessionGitState lines 1553-1554 always computes state, and _computeSessionGitState lines 1888-1906 runs all probes at repositoryRoot. agentHostSchema.ts lines 1178-1182 defaults gitCoalesceReads to false.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve each additional folder's cached checkout root and group its Git-state read by normalized root and base-branch input, then apply the shared result to each folder scope. Keep primary reads with a different configured base separate and preserve per-folder non-repository classification.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new code materializes the entire directory and synchronously sorts it before the first loop-body budget check or file/directory filter. The budget charges one readdir operation, not entries or comparisons. The exact pause depends on directory size, but the unbounded allocation and synchronous O(N log N) work are directly established.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Dirent objects and strings for the whole directory, sort temporary storage, and synchronous localeCompare comparisons on the agent-host event loop
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A scanned directory containing N entries allocates O(N) objects and performs O(N log N) comparisons. The 10,000-probe and five-second start-deadline budgets do not bound N; one readdir consumes only one probe. The work repeats on rediscovery after 60 seconds, or eligible forced refreshes after 30 seconds.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Agent-host event-loop stalls and memory/GC spikes despite repository discovery being scheduled in the background
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Session Git-state refreshes did not enumerate and sort scanned subdirectories for repository discovery.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each scanned directory is fully materialized and sorted, including every ordinary file, even when no repository can be found there or the discovery deadline expired during readdir.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 502-503 read all Dirents using readdir and immediately sort them with localeCompare. Added lines 504-509 check done() and reject ordinary files only after sorting. Repository discovery and this work did not exist in the base revision.
Findings.Title: Bound directory entries before allocating and sorting them
Findings.Impact: Scanning a large generated-output, dataset, or cache directory containing tens or hundreds of thousands of files blocks other agent-host requests while sorting entries that are then all discarded as non-directories. A deep or unlimited-depth detection setting can reach such folders.
Findings.Evidence: findRepositories lines 399-400 defines done() and charges each boundary call once. Lines 502-509 materialize and sort entries before checking done() or entry.isDirectory(). The discovery caller supplies a shared 10,000-probe/five-second budget and revisits the scan via _refreshSessionRepositories. Existing worktreeDiskUsage.ts lines 183-194 demonstrates fs.opendir-based incremental directory iteration in this subsystem.
Findings.Recommendation: Use bounded directory iteration, charge/check the entry budget while consuming results, and sort only a bounded set of eligible directory candidates. Stop before allocating or sorting the rest of a huge directory when the deadline or entry cap is reached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Existing single-folder session without repository detection options
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The source checkout's base-branch lookup, Git-state computation, existing state persistence, and any existing branch-change PR lookup precede the refresh event. Both new helpers take their empty fast paths when nothing was previously recorded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository root and run status, remote listing, symbolic-ref, and optional base/upstream probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One checkout computation, three initial commands; a root-cache miss adds one rev-parse and a directory stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same primary-checkout computation occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing authoritative checkout work remains awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the configured base branch and persist changed primary Git state through the session-state store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One base lookup per refresh; writes occur when primary state changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same persistence path was used before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing reads and primary-state saves can precede publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One primary working directory; no additional folders or discovered roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh requests are merged and serialized per session key with a five-second cooldown. gitCoalesceReads defaults false. When enabled, only READ_ONLY_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS use the eight-read limiter; remote and symbolic-ref are not in that set and bypass it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing repository-root positive/negative LRU cache and in-flight root lookup remain. No discovery cache or repository bookkeeping is populated without options and prior metadata. The state read itself is not a persistent result cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the empty guards and explicit pre/post diff comparison.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No performance measurement was performed; there is no added scaling work on this fast path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression for the unchanged single-folder/no-options fast path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete Discard or another Git-changing changeset operation after repository discovery has warmed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The handler finishes its mutation, then _executeChangesetOperation awaits _refreshGitState before publishing Idle and returning. The primary/session checkout refresh now additionally awaits passive folder reads and warm-cache discovered-root reads before completing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read passive checkouts' root-wide Git status, remotes, default branch, and optional divergence information.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three initial commands for each selected distinct checkout, up to 48 additional initial commands when F+U=16, plus optional probes. Ordinary confirmed non-repositories start zero Git commands; forced retries add one root probe each.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Operation completion awaited the source/session checkout refresh, not these passive checkouts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All selected state reads are awaited before operation status becomes Idle; one unrelated slow checkout can delay the operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat uncached folders and re-probe roots after inconclusive state reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Root-cache misses perform one directory stat and root probe; an inconclusive discovered-root read performs a fresh root check, sequentially in the result loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unrelated additional/discovered folders were not classified on operation completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These classification checks are inside the newly awaited passive path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Encode live folder Git/GitHub maps and publish session metadata envelopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only changed folder state schedules saves; up to F+U state updates per application, with existing per-session save sequencers and metadata actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic passive-folder state updates were issued by the session refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Passive saves are deliberately not awaited by the refresh; synchronous metadata updates still occur before it returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S non-scratch session folders; F eligible additional folders after chat-scope exclusion, capped at 16; U unique discovered roots after excluding session-folder scopes, bounded by min(16,max(0,17-S)). F+U is at most 16 per refresh application.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Additional-folder reads run as one Promise.all batch after the primary read; discovered-root reads run as a subsequent Promise.all batch. Default configuration launches Git reads without the optional limiter. With coalescing enabled, status and other listed shareable reads use an eight-slot global limiter, but remote -v and symbolic-ref bypass it. Session refresh requests remain serialized/coalesced per key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold discovery runs in the background. Warm discovery reuses the inventory but not Git-state results: _applyDiscoveredRepositories still computes each selected root's state. Simultaneous compatible URI/base reads join in-flight promises; completed reads are forgotten. Forced reads do not reuse earlier ordinary reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added awaits, warm-cache branch, Promise.all, changesGitState=true for Discard, and operation Running-to-Idle ordering are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Checkout size, disk speed, and timeout prevalence determine duration; the default per-command timeout is 30 seconds. The critical-path extension is statically proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the newly awaited passive-repository work on existing operation completion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh a multi-root workspace containing several packages in the same monorepo checkout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A session refresh computes primary state, then enumerates additional eligible working-directory URIs and waits for each state computation. File-monitor events can repeatedly reach this path after their existing debounce and the refresh cooldown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute root-wide Git state separately for every additional package folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Default behavior issues 3F initial commands for one effective checkout/default-base group, up to 48, plus the primary read and optional probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The session refresh computed the primary checkout once rather than automatically computing it again for each package folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repeated full status traversals contend on the same checkout and all belong to the awaited refresh batch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each package folder to its checkout root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Warm exact-folder cache hits avoid probes; cold distinct folder keys can each require a stat/root lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Additional package paths were not automatically resolved and read during the session refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Root resolution precedes each duplicate state computation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F distinct additional folder URIs sharing one checkout root, F<=16 after scratch/chat exclusions. Their effective root/default-base group count is one, not F independent repositories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: With the default false gitCoalesceReads setting, F computations start in parallel and issue F status, F remote, and F symbolic-ref commands. With the setting enabled, overlapping status reads share or use the global eight-read limiter; the 2F remote/symbolic-ref commands still bypass that limiter. A primary read with a configured base must remain separate from the additional default-base group.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm root caches identify the same checkout. _readGitState nevertheless uses the original folder URI plus base input, so these different URI keys do not join. There is no completed Git-state result cache. Enabling command-level coalescing can share overlapping status/default-base commands, but remote and symbolic-ref are not shareable and remain duplicated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the test demonstrates shared checkout roots, URI-keyed coalescing fails to group them, and all Git probes run at the resolved root.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of package folders and cost of root-wide status determine the overhead. Same-checkout workspaces are explicitly represented by a newly added test.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported redundant additional-folder state computations; grouping by normalized checkout root and base input preserves folder-scoped state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover nested repositories and recursive submodules in a large directory tree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Discovery is off the session refresh's cold critical path. However, its synchronous directory sorting executes on the same agent-host event loop, delaying unrelated requests. Own-root probes occur before the shared scan deadline is created.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read whole directories, lstat Git markers/path components, and read bounded .gitmodules files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 10,000 charged scan boundary calls and no new charged call after the five-second deadline; a single readdir nevertheless allocates all N directory entries, and sorting costs O(N log N). .gitmodules content is checked against 64 KiB before reading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No repository-discovery directory enumeration or sorting occurred in session refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async traversal is background work; synchronous sorting blocks the host event loop despite background scheduling and can occur before the next deadline check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fresh own-root rev-parse and rev-parse --show-cdup for directories with .git entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 16 own-root probes before the scan budget; one charged Git check for each candidate .git marker encountered, included in the scan-probe cap. Accepted root count is lower than candidate count when markers are invalid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only Git probes needed for the primary source checkout were performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the cold refresh critical path, but shares process/disk resources and optional shareable-read limiter with interactive work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 16 session folders are root-probed. Host discovery accepts at most 16 distinct additional roots across folders; the scanner has its own 64-result safety cap, depth cap 10, 10,000 shared boundary probes, and up to 64 submodule declarations per bounded .gitmodules file. N entries in a single scanned directory are not capped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One discovery per session; latest changed input is queued while a scan runs. Up to 16 own-root probes start in parallel, then folder scans and candidate checks run sequentially against one shared budget. Optional eight-read limiting applies to rev-parse/status shareable reads only. Synchronous sort has no yielding or entry budget.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovery inventory is keyed by current folders and detection options. It is reused until stale, input changes, 60 seconds have passed on a refresh, or an eligible forced refresh is at least 30 seconds later. Own roots are re-read fresh. Within a scan, seen/expanded/scannedPaths deduplicate successful roots, submodule expansion, and explicit scan paths. Ignored names and roots, .git paths, and symlinks are skipped.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: readdir and sort precede both done() and directory filtering, so probe/time limits cannot bound per-directory allocation or sort work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large output/cache/dataset directories depend on scan depth and ignored-folder settings. No measured stall duration is claimed; allocation and comparison growth are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported unbounded directory materialization/sorting. Existing depth/probe/root/submodule caps and serial scan scheduling otherwise bound traversal fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Attach pull requests to newly read additional folders and discovered repositories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Additional-folder PR lookups and persistence are deliberately scheduled without awaiting them in the session refresh. The primary session's existing PR lookup can still be awaited on its own branch change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List pull requests by head branch; when empty and HEAD exists, list pull requests associated with that commit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One branch-list request per distinct eligible account/repository/head query after in-flight grouping; at most one commit-list fallback per lookup. Commit results are limited to the first 100; branch lookup asks for one result. Existing transport retry policies may add attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automatic session refresh did not look up PRs for additional session folders/discovered roots; primary and chat lookups already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the new passive refresh critical path and globally scheduled by the transport.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: rev-parse HEAD before commit-associated PR fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per empty branch lookup with a working directory; compatible concurrent Git reads can share when command coalescing is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This fallback existed for primary/chat lookups but was not invoked for automatically read additional folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the passive refresh critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize folder maps, update central state, and mirror changed metadata to legacy session/chat databases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Changed folders schedule per-session sequenced saves; writes go through the existing central store and legacy mirror scheduler. Mirror changes are grouped by storage resource; they are not independent synchronous flushes per folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same store/mirror infrastructure existed, but these automatically discovered folder-state updates were absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Passive saves are not awaited by refresh or next lookup; persistence remains sequenced per session.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to 16 additional/discovered Git-state reads per application. Only folders whose GitHub repository or branch changed enqueue an automatic lookup. Effective network grouping is by compatible account/URL/query after transport in-flight coalescing; distinct repositories or branches remain distinct requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Lookups serialize per session+folder key, not across all folders. Underlying RequestQueue defaults to 12 overall/host, 10 per account, and 8 per caller, with reserved interactive admission and rate-limit backpressure. Each lookup performs branch lookup before optional HEAD/commit fallback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already-associated branch skips lookup. Empty or failed lookup is not automatically retried on every unchanged refresh because enqueueing is gated by repository/branch change. Transport shares compatible in-flight GETs and uses ETag revalidation for completed responses; warm ETags do not eliminate the network call. API clients are shared/referenced and disposed after resolution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the gates, ordering, transport grouping, queue limits, and disposal path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number of non-base branches and PR fallback misses controls network work. Global scheduling/coalescing prevents inferring one simultaneous network request per folder.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence regression reported for the intentional background PR lookups; did not mistake per-folder sequencers for absence of transport-level limits.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change detection options, remove folders/repositories, or remove a session while discovery is running
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An options change schedules a normal coalesced Git refresh. Outdated discoveries and stale state reads are rejected before recording. Cleanup metadata/save work is backgrounded; the authoritative refresh still runs according to its existing lane.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry negative roots on a forced refresh and fresh-check roots after inconclusive Git reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Ordinary confirmed negative additional folders issue zero root probes; a forced retry issues one per selected negative folder, at most 16. Discovered-root failures can issue one fresh classification probe each.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These additional/discovered roots were not automatically reclassified by the session refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Classification is in the newly awaited passive refresh, already covered by the operation-latency finding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove old folder-scope Git/GitHub entries and publish changed metadata through the existing state-manager envelope path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by prior recorded additional/discovered entries; unchanged state does not schedule new removal updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no discovery-owned additional state to remove.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: In-memory cleanup occurs during refresh/application; persistence is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active discovery plus one latest pending credential/input request per session, up to 16 root probes and the shared bounded scan. Session-owned maps are keyed by session and deleted on removal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session discovery is serialized and pending changes collapse to the latest input. Reads already started are not canceled solely because the session/options disappeared; their completion is guarded. Existing scan budget bounds further issuance, though a started filesystem operation may outlive its deadline.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Input signatures and generation counters prevent stale recording. Removing options removes discovery inventory and previous discovered metadata; vanished checkouts mark inventory stale. Known non-repositories avoid ordinary root probes and are retried once on forced refresh. Removal clears discovery/pending/generation/additional-folder maps.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cache invalidation, generation checks, latest-input coalescing, and session-removal map cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Slow already-started disk calls can outlive the five-second issuance budget, but no unbounded queue or lost lifecycle ownership was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional cleanup/retention finding. Correctness-only stale-state questions were excluded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed performance-review over all 17 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted three introduced regressions: warm passive reads block changeset completion, same-checkout additional folders repeat root-wide Git computations, and directory sorting bypasses entry/time bounds. Final concurrency assessment: the optional global eight-read limiter only covers the read-only subcommand allowlist; remote and symbolic-ref bypass it even when coalescing is enabled. Reviewed negative caching, discovery input/generation guards, save/mirror sequencing, transport request grouping and limits, and session-removal cleanup. No concrete pre-existing performance regression fixed by this PR met the provenance-reporting threshold. Static read-only review; magnitude is unmeasured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
